[[File:NC Courage vs KC Current (Sep 2024) 030.jpg|thumb|right|350px|{{center|Week 18 starting lineup:<br/>[[Nichelle Prince|Prince]], [[Ellie Wheeler|Wheeler]], [[Temwa Chawinga|Chawinga]], [[Alana Cook|Cook]], [[Hailie Mace|Mace]], [[Stine Ballisager Pedersen|Ballisager]]<br/>[[Vanessa DiBernardo|DiBernardo]], [[Bayley Feist|Feist]], [[Almuth Schult|Schult]], [[Lo'eau LaBonta|LaBonta]], [[Debinha]]}}]]

The '''2024 [[Kansas City Current]] season''' was the team's fourth season as a professional [[women's association football|soccer team]]. The Current played in the [[National Women's Soccer League]] (NWSL), the top tier of [[women's soccer in the United States]].

The Current finished fourth in the [[2024 National Women's Soccer League season]] and qualified for the [[NWSL playoffs]] as the fourth seed, where they defeated the fifth-seeded [[North Carolina Courage]] in the quarterfinals before losing to the top-seeded [[Orlando Pride]] in the semifinals.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/42450783/marta-pride-kc-current-nwsl-final-spirit |title=Marta, Pride down K.C. Current to set up NWSL final with Spirit |date=November 17, 2024 |access-date=November 17, 2024 |first1=Jeff |last1=Kassouf |work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

== Background ==
{{main|2023 Kansas City Current season}}

Despite making it to the championship match in the 2022 season, the Current did not qualify for the 2023 playoffs. They ended the [[2023 National Women's Soccer League season|2023 regular season]] 11th out of 12 teams. In 2021, they ended their [[2021 National Women's Soccer League season|inaugural season]] in last place.

== Summary ==

=== Draft, trades, and transfers ===
{{See also|#Transactions}}

==== NWSL Draft ====
{{see also|#2024 NWSL Draft}}
In the 2024 NWSL Draft, the KC Current drafted [[Ellie Wheeler]] from [[Penn State Nittany Lions women's soccer|Penn State]], Halle Mackiewicz from [[Clemson Tigers women's soccer|Clemson]], and Hope Hisey from [[Arizona Wildcats women's soccer|Arizona]].

== Stadium and facilities ==
The KC Current began playing in their new home stadium, [[CPKC Stadium]], the first stadium in the world stadium built solely for a women's professional sports team. The stadium has a seating capacity of 11,500 with additional standing-room capacity on its north-end. The stadium is located in the Berkley Riverfront of Kansas City along the banks of the [[Missouri River]], the namesake of the team.

CPKC Stadium held its first match between the Kansas City Current and the [[Portland Thorns]] on March 16, 2024. Kansas City won the match 5–4 in front of a sell-out crowd.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/39747209/kansas-city-current-open-women-specific-nwsl-stadium-portland|title=Kansas City Current open 'game-changing' stadium with 5-4 win|website=ESPN.com|last=Kassouf|first=Jeff|date=March 16, 2024|access-date=March 16, 2024|language=en}}</ref>

The Current continue to train in their dedicated practice facility in [[Riverside, Missouri]], which opened in June 2022. It was the first purpose-built practice facility for an NWSL team.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.insider.com/kansas-city-current-million-dollar-training-complex-nwsl-photos-2022-6 |title=Kansas City Current's sparkling new $18 million facility shows the luxury women's pro athletes have long missed out on |date=June 25, 2022 |access-date=July 20, 2022 |publisher=[[Business Insider|Insider]] |first=Meredith |last=Cash}}</ref>

=== Playoffs ===
{{main|2024 National Women's Soccer League season#Playoffs}}

The Current finished the regular season in fourth place and qualified for the NWSL playoffs as the fourth seed of eight teams.
